questions.q: What does a Pod's resource 'request' actually control?
options: The hard maximum the Pod is ever allowed to use
The amount of CPU/memory the scheduler reserves when deciding whether a node has room to place the Pod
The amount of disk storage the Pod can request dynamically
The number of replicas the Pod can scale to
questions.explain: A request is a placement guarantee used by the scheduler — it only places a Pod on a node with enough unreserved capacity to cover the request. It is not itself a usage cap.

questions.q: A checkout container exceeds its memory limit. What happens?
options: The container is throttled and slowed down but keeps running
The container is OOMKilled and restarted, because memory cannot be throttled back once allocated
Nothing happens — memory limits are advisory only
The Pod is evicted from the cluster permanently with no restart
questions.explain: Memory is incompressible, so a container that exceeds its memory limit is OOMKilled (out-of-memory killed) and restarted, rather than throttled.

questions.q: How does exceeding a CPU limit differ from exceeding a memory limit?
options: They behave identically — both result in the container being killed
CPU overage results in throttling (the container is slowed down but keeps running); memory overage results in OOMKill
CPU overage kills the container; memory overage only throttles it
Neither CPU nor memory limits have any enforced effect
questions.explain: CPU is a compressible resource — exceeding the CPU limit throttles the container rather than killing it. Memory is incompressible, so exceeding its limit triggers an OOMKill.

questions.q: Northbridge sets requests.cpu == limits.cpu AND requests.memory == limits.memory for the checkout container. What QoS class does this Pod get?
options: BestEffort
Burstable
Guaranteed
Priority
questions.explain: Guaranteed QoS requires requests to equal limits for both CPU and memory on every container in the Pod. Guaranteed Pods are evicted last under node resource pressure.

questions.q: A Pod has no resources.requests or resources.limits set at all. What QoS class does it receive, and what does that mean under node resource pressure?
options: Guaranteed — it is protected from eviction
Burstable — it is evicted before Guaranteed Pods but after BestEffort
BestEffort — it is the first to be evicted when a node runs low on resources
The Pod fails to schedule without resource settings
questions.explain: A Pod with no requests or limits at all gets the BestEffort QoS class, making it the first candidate for eviction when a node comes under resource pressure.
